title: Mission: find what you downloaded
drDigitalIntro:
Downloading something is easy. Finding it afterwards is where people get stuck, and it is the whole difference between a computer that feels useful and one that feels like it eats things.
• You will download a small file from this page and then hand the same file back, which you can only do by finding it in your own Downloads folder.
• The file is called Downloads-Practice.pdf. If you pick anything else, the page will say so.
• You will also read this page's real web address out of the address bar and type it back.
• Nothing is uploaded. The file stays on your computer; the page only reads its name.

playgroundTask.goal: You found your own Downloads folder and read your own address bar

download.label: Download the practice file
download.note: A one-page PDF, about 1 KB. It exists purely so you can go and find it again.

steps.say: Read the address bar at the top of this browser and type the address of this page.
steps.detail: Just the part before the first slash — the site's own name. That strip at the top is the only part of a page a website cannot fake.
Your browser will save it without asking, or ask you where to put it. Either way, notice where it says it went.

steps.say: Find Downloads-Practice.pdf on your computer and hand it back.
steps.detail: Press Choose a file, then find your Downloads folder in the side of the window that opens. This is the step that proves a download is never lost — it is in a folder, with a name.

steps.say: Open a new tab and go to a site you know by typing its address.
steps.detail: Type it straight into the address bar rather than searching for it. If you know the address, searching first is a detour that scam sites rely on.

steps.say: Find the padlock in the address bar on a site where you sign in.
steps.detail: The padlock means the line between you and that site is private. It does not mean the site is honest — but its absence, on a page asking for a password, is a reason to stop.

drDigitalSuccess: You downloaded a file, went and found it, and read the real address of the page you were on. Those two habits between them prevent most of the trouble beginners have online.
drDigitalHint: If the file check says the name is wrong, you have picked a different file. Look for Downloads-Practice.pdf specifically, in the Downloads folder.
